item.title: Edgar Allan Poe's Interactive Horror: 1995 Edition Review |Terminal Gamer
item.description: TG writes: Step into a fog-choked 1995 manor where William S. Burroughs growls Poes darkest tales while dead-eyed clay puppets watch your every move. In Edgar Allan Poe's Interactive Horror: 1995 Edition, guilt and madness swallow you whole in a raw, unsettling descent that feels more like possession than gameplay.
